findings.title: Potential Reentrancy
findings.description: External call is made before state is updated. An attacker can re-enter the function and drain funds before the balance is recorded.
findings.recommendation: Follow Checks-Effects-Interactions: update state (SSTORE) before making external calls, or use a reentrancy guard.

findings.title: User-Controlled Storage Write
findings.description: [Taint Analysis] SSTORE is called with a value or slot derived from user input. An attacker may be able to overwrite arbitrary storage slots.
findings.recommendation: Validate and sanitize all user-supplied values before writing to storage. Use Solidity 0.8+ or SafeMath.

findings.title: User-Controlled Call Target
findings.description: [Taint Analysis] The destination address of a CALL is derived from user input. An attacker can redirect ETH or execution to an arbitrary contract.
findings.recommendation: Never use user-supplied addresses as call targets without strict validation.

findings.title: Unchecked Call Return Value
findings.description: CALL return value is never checked. A failed call will be silently ignored, potentially losing ETH or causing incorrect state.
findings.recommendation: Check the return value: (bool success,) = addr.call{value: x}(''); require(success);

findings.title: Timestamp Dependence
findings.description: block.timestamp is used in a conditional branch. Miners can manipulate timestamps by up to 15 seconds to influence the outcome.
findings.recommendation: Avoid using block.timestamp for randomness or critical logic. Use block.number for relative timing, or Chainlink VRF for randomness.

findings.title: Possible Integer Overflow
findings.description: ADD or MUL is used near state changes without bounds checks in 57 location(s). Contracts compiled before Solidity 0.8 have no built-in overflow protection.
findings.recommendation: Use Solidity 0.8+ which reverts on overflow by default, or SafeMath for older versions.

findings.title: Integer Overflow Leading to Storage Corruption
findings.description: [Taint Analysis] An unchecked arithmetic operation on user input flows directly into SSTORE. An attacker can cause an integer overflow to manipulate storage values, potentially stealing funds or taking ownership.
findings.recommendation: Validate and sanitize all user-supplied values before writing to storage. Use Solidity 0.8+ or SafeMath.
